summary: Photonics M.Sc. student and LMU astrophysics graduate focused on astronomical instrumentation, wavefront sensing and optical-system performance, combining optical modelling, experimental apparatus development and astronomical data analysis.

details: Selected coursework: Physical Optics and Modelling (Zemax optical design); Micro and Fiber Optics; Optical Measurement Technology; Semiconductor Optics and Components.
Grade: 1.55 (German scale). Selected coursework: Essentials of Advanced Astrophysics; Cosmology and Structure Formation; Statistical Methods; Instrumental Laboratory Courses.
Electronics, control systems and embedded systems.

core.title: Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensing & Adaptive Optics Simulation
bullets: Developed a modular Python SCAO framework connecting atmospheric turbulence, detector-level Shack-Hartmann sensing, calibrated reconstruction, deformable-mirror correction and delayed feedback.
Investigated detector-noise and gain/latency trade-offs using residual wavefront error, propagated-PSF Strehl and encircled energy.
Diagnosed a reconstruction failure associated with measurement dropout in a 2.2 m NGS model; stronger TSVD regularisation kept reconstruction usable throughout the matched two-second run.
Cross-checked selected optical components against HCIPy and analytic references; documented reproducible experiments, model limitations and an interactive explorer of recorded results.

core.title: Weak Lensing Void Finder
core.supervisors: Prof. Joseph Mohr and Dr. Chris Davies
bullets: Developed and parameter-tested a watershed finder for cosmic voids in 2D full-sky weak-lensing convergence maps.
Applied the analysis to DES Y3 weak-lensing maps; characterised void abundance, effective radii, ellipticities and convergence profiles.

core.title: Experimental Collisional Charging Apparatus
core.supervisors: Prof. Gerhard Wurm and Dr. Felix Jungmann
bullets: Designed the mechanical apparatus in CAD, fabricated components by 3D printing and assembled the setup; integrated and debugged electronic charge-measurement modules.
Conducted measurements and analysed grain-size dependence of collisional charging, testing a dust-collision growth hypothesis relevant to early planet formation.

labs: Tested static and dynamic correction on LMU's ALPAO bench in July 2022 using a Shack-Hartmann sensor and deformable mirror. Other labs covered CCD imaging and reduction, optical interferometry and radio measurements of Galactic rotation.

Measured laser beam quality (M²), shaped ultrashort pulses and characterised them by autocorrelation. Fibre experiments covered OTDR, polarisation, Bragg gratings and coupling. Also worked on APD measurements, laser spectra, laser interferometry and nonlinear optics.
Took and processed images with my supervisor at Wendelstein (43 cm).

additional.title: Astrophotonics
bullets: Modelled how AO wavefront error, injection jitter and photonic-lantern mode count affect fiber coupling, spectral SNR and radial-velocity precision.

bullets: Reproduced the 5 arcmin RMS wavefront error to 0.3% and traced a 27 percentage-point ensquared-energy discrepancy to the choice of focal surface.
